body_text:
Well-ordering principle for the natural numbers. Every nonempty
subset of $\mathbb{N}$ has a least element. This principle is
equivalent to induction. For if an inductive claim failed, the set
of counterexamples would have a least element; the base case and
induction step exclude both possibilities for that least
counterexample.
